content.json:
The data lake stores security data outside the Analytics tier and is billed on five separate meters. This workbook can estimate mirrored storage volume from workspace data, but it cannot produce a complete data lake cost estimate because several meters are not recorded in the Analytics workspace.

This section can derive the following from mirrored workspace `Usage` volume:

- Mirrored volume size by table
- Retained raw log size based on the selected Analytics and total lake retention assumptions
- Billed compressed log size using the documented **6:1** compression ratio
- Estimated lake storage cost for the selected time range, using the storage price parameter

The following meters are not visible in the Analytics workspace and are not modeled in this workbook:

- Data lake ingestion: monthly GB ingested into tables set to data lake tier only
- Data processing: monthly GB processed for lake-tier-only tables, including transformations such as redaction, splitting, filtering, and normalization
- Data lake query: monthly GB of uncompressed data scanned by KQL queries and jobs against the lake
- Advanced data insights: monthly notebook and job compute hours

When the data lake is enabled, Analytics-tier data is **mirrored** to the lake at no extra ingestion charge, so mirrored volume is visible in `Usage` and is used for the storage estimate. Ingestion and data processing are charged only for tables set to **data lake tier only**; that data never reaches the Analytics workspace. Query charges depend on GB scanned and insights charges on notebook compute hours, neither of which is recorded in `Usage`.

Storage is billed on compressed data and applies only to data still retained after the Analytics retention period ends. These are planning estimates, not invoice values.

Validate in **Microsoft Sentinel > Cost management** in the Microsoft Defender portal, and review the [data lake overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/datalake/sentinel-lake-overview), [billing model](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing#understand-the-full-billing-model-for-microsoft-sentinel), and [cost monitoring guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing-monitor-costs).

parameters.name: LakeStoragePrice
parameters.label: Lake storage price (per compressed GB/month)
parameters.description: Data lake storage rate per compressed GB per month. Storage is billed at a 6:1 compression ratio on data retained after Analytics retention ends.

parameters.name: LakeAnalyticsRetentionDays
parameters.label: Analytics retention (days)
parameters.description: Analytics-tier retention in days. Lake storage is charged only for data retained beyond this period.

paramValidationRules.message: Enter a whole number of days greater than zero.

parameters.name: LakeTotalRetentionMonths
parameters.label: Total lake retention (months)
parameters.description: Total retention in the data lake tier, up to 12 years (144 months).

paramValidationRules.message: Enter a whole number of months greater than zero.

content.json:
Microsoft documents the following Sentinel data sources as free:

- Azure Activity Logs (`AzureActivity`)
- Health monitoring for Microsoft Sentinel (`SentinelHealth`)
- Microsoft 365 audit activity (`OfficeActivity`)
- Microsoft Entra ID Protection alerts (`SecurityAlert`)
- Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Defender for IoT alerts (`SecurityAlert`)
- Microsoft Defender XDR incidents and alerts (`SecurityIncident`, `SecurityAlert`)
- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Identity, Cloud Apps, and Office 365 alerts (`SecurityAlert`)

This section estimates Analytics-tier ingestion in the selected workspace scope and keeps it separate from billable ingestion. It does not estimate data lake-only ingestion, storage, processing, or query charges. Usage is grouped by table and cannot reliably identify the originating connector, so `SecurityAlert` cannot be allocated reliably among its contributing services. This estimate does not calculate the separate Sentinel free trial. Review the [Microsoft Sentinel free data sources](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing?tabs=simplified%2Ccommitment-tiers#free-data-sources) documentation for current eligibility and billing terms.

content.json:
Qualifying Microsoft 365 E7, E5, A5, F5, and G5 licenses, and corresponding Security licenses, may receive a Microsoft Sentinel data grant of up to 5 MB per qualifying user per day for eligible Microsoft 365 data.

Eligible data-source groups include:

- Microsoft Entra ID sign-in and audit logs (`SigninLogs`, `AuditLogs`, `AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs`, `AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, `AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs`, `AADProvisioningLogs`, `ADFSSignInLogs`, `AADUserRiskEvents`, `AADRiskyUsers`)
- Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps Guard shadow IT discovery logs (`McasShadowItReporting`)
- Microsoft Purview Information Protection logs (`InformationProtectionLogs_CL`)
- Microsoft 365 advanced hunting data (the eligible `Device*`, `Email*`, `Identity*`, `AlertEvidence`, and `CloudAppEvents` tables shown below)

This workbook estimates the Analytics-tier ingestion benefit from billable Usage data in the selected workspace scope. It does not estimate data lake-only charges or prove that a row came from an eligible connector, that the offer applies to your agreement, or that the calculated amount matches billing. The grant cap is modeled once across the selected scope; it is not multiplied per workspace.

Review the [Microsoft 365 Sentinel benefit offer](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/offers/sentinel-microsoft-365-offer/) for current eligibility, agreement terms, and supported data types. Enter **Total Microsoft 365 E7/E5/A5/F5/G5 seats** below and use the global **Ingestion price** to calculate the estimate.

content.title: Microsoft Sentinel benefit for Defender for Servers Plan 2

content.json:
Defender for Servers Plan 2 provides up to 500 MB of eligible Analytics-tier ingestion per protected server or node per day. The allowance is pooled across machines in each subscription and applied at workspace level. This workbook estimates observed usage; it does not prove Plan 2 protection, licensing, eligibility, or data lake-only charges.

Core eligible tables:

- `SecurityAlert`, `SecurityBaseline`, `SecurityBaselineSummary`, `SecurityDetection`, `SecurityEvent`
- `WindowsFirewall`, `ProtectionStatus`, `MDCFileIntegrityMonitoringEvents`
- `DeviceCustomFileEvents`, `DeviceCustomRegistryEvents`

Conditionally eligible tables:

- `Update`, `UpdateSummary`: review the applicable Update Management conditions
- `WindowsEvent`: only security data from the Microsoft-SecurityEvent stream

Nodes is the distinct `Computer` count observed in `Heartbeat`, not proof of licensing or Plan 2 protection. Review the [Defender for Servers Plan 2 data ingestion benefit](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/defender-for-cloud/data-ingestion-benefit) for current eligibility and terms.

content.json: This section estimates Analytics-tier charges for billable data retained longer than 90 days, using historical billable workspace records. XDR and data lake retention use separate billing models. Review [Manage data tiers and retention in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/manage-data-overview) for retention and data-tier guidance.

parameters.name: RetentionPrice
parameters.label: Retention price
parameters.description: Enter the retention price per GB/month used for this section's estimates.

content.query: let retainedDataGB = toreal(coalesce(toscalar((union withsource = SourceTableName * | where TimeGenerated < startofday(now()) - 90d | where _IsBillable == true | summarize sum(_BilledSize) / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0)), 0.0)); print ['Average Daily Retention Cost'] = retainedDataGB * todouble('{RetentionPrice}') / 30.0

content.json:
Microsoft Sentinel and Log Analytics offer Pay-As-You-Go and Commitment Tier pricing. This section automatically detects the current workspace tier and calculates a **usage-based suggested tier** from average billable daily ingestion over the last 31 days.

> **New workspace notice:** A recommendation is shown only after 31 days of billable data are detected. Until then, the table reports how many days remain before the recommendation becomes available; a shorter history cannot accurately represent the fixed 31-day review period.

> **Estimate only:** The suggested tier uses ingestion volume, not actual pricing. It is not the Azure portal **Recommended Tier** and should not be used as the sole basis for a pricing change. Azure evaluates each available tier using the prior 31 days and your applicable pricing to identify the lowest estimated-cost option. Review [Usage and estimated costs in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/change-pricing-tier#changing-pricing-tier) before changing a tier.

Review **Days since tier last changed** before making a change: a commitment tier has a 31-day period during which it cannot move to a lower commitment or consumption tier. Confirm rates on the [Microsoft Sentinel pricing page](https://www.microsoft.com/security/pricing/microsoft-sentinel/) and review [Plan costs and understand pricing and billing for Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing?tabs=simplified%2Ccommitment-tiers#analytics-tier).

parameters.name: CurrentCommitmentTier
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces'
| where id in~ ({Workspace}) or 'value::all' in~ ({Workspace})
| extend skuName = tolower(tostring(properties.sku.name)), capacityReservationLevel = toint(properties.sku.capacityReservationLevel)
| extend currentTier = case(skuName == 'capacityreservation', strcat(tostring(capacityReservationLevel), ' GB/day commitment'), skuName == 'pergb2018', 'Pay-As-You-Go', skuName == 'free', 'Free tier', skuName == 'standalone', 'Standalone tier', skuName == 'standard', 'Standard tier', skuName == 'premium', 'Premium tier', 'Unknown')
| summarize WorkspaceCount = dcount(id), CurrentTier = any(currentTier)
| project CurrentCommitmentTier = iif(WorkspaceCount == 1, CurrentTier, 'Multiple workspaces')

content.query: let reviewDays = 31.0; let reviewStart = ago(31d); let historyProbeStart = ago(32d); let currentTier = '{CurrentCommitmentTier}'; let tierLevels = dynamic([50,100,200,300,400,500,1000,2000,5000]); union withsource = SourceTableName * | where TimeGenerated between (historyProbeStart .. now()) | where _IsBillable == true | summarize TotalBilledBytes = sumif(_BilledSize, TimeGenerated >= reviewStart), FirstObserved = min(TimeGenerated) | extend ObservedHistoryDays = iif(isnull(FirstObserved), 0.0, min_of(reviewDays, datetime_diff('second', now(), FirstObserved) / 86400.0)) | extend DaysRemaining = toint(ceiling(max_of(reviewDays - ObservedHistoryDays, 0.0))) | extend AvgDailyGB = iif(DaysRemaining == 0, TotalBilledBytes / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / reviewDays, real(null)), TierLevels = tierLevels | mv-expand TierLevel = TierLevels to typeof(int) | extend IsEligible = TierLevel >= AvgDailyGB | summarize SuggestedTierGBPerDay = minif(TierLevel, IsEligible), AvgDailyGB = any(AvgDailyGB), ObservedHistoryDays = any(ObservedHistoryDays), DaysRemaining = any(DaysRemaining) | extend suggestedTier = case(DaysRemaining > 0, strcat('Ready in ', tostring(DaysRemaining), iif(DaysRemaining == 1, ' day', ' days')), AvgDailyGB < 50.0, 'Pay-As-You-Go', isnotempty(SuggestedTierGBPerDay), strcat(tostring(SuggestedTierGBPerDay), ' GB/day commitment'), 'Above 5000 GB/day - review Azure portal options') | extend alignmentStatus = case(DaysRemaining > 0, 'Not Ready', currentTier == 'Not available' or currentTier == 'Unknown' or currentTier == 'Multiple workspaces', 'Not evaluated', suggestedTier startswith 'Above 5000 GB/day', 'Review in portal', currentTier == suggestedTier, 'Aligned', 'Review tier') | project Current = currentTier, Suggested = suggestedTier, Status = alignmentStatus, ['Avg daily GB'] = round(AvgDailyGB, 2)
content.title: Usage-based suggested tier details
content.noDataMessage: No billable ingestion was found in the last 31 days.

content.json:
Microsoft Sentinel playbooks use Azure Logic Apps to automate responses to incidents, alerts, and other security operations workflows. This section discovers accessible Logic Apps across the selected subscription and resource group scope.

All matching Logic Apps are included by default. Use the subscription, resource group, and Logic Apps controls to narrow the scope. The table below lists the Logic Apps included by the selected parameters.

Billable execution metrics are not shown in this table: Logic Apps execution data lives in `AzureMetrics`, which is frequently configured as a Basic Logs table and cannot be queried through the Logs experience these panels use (the query returns 'Basic Logs table is not supported in Logs'). Review billable executions in the Logic App **Metrics** blade (metrics `BillableActionExecutions` and `BillableTriggerExecutions`), Azure Monitor metrics, or Cost Management.

Review [Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/automation/automate-responses-with-playbooks) for playbook guidance. Because playbooks use Azure Logic Apps, additional charges can apply. Go to the [Azure Logic Apps](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/logic-apps/) pricing page for more details.

parameters.name: ResourceGroups
parameters.label: Resource groups
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type in~ ({ResourceTypes})
| summarize Count = count() by subscriptionId, resourceGroup
| order by Count desc
| project value = strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup), label = resourceGroup

parameters.name: Resources
parameters.label: Logic Apps
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type in~ ({ResourceTypes})
| extend resourceGroupId = strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup)
| where resourceGroupId in~ ({ResourceGroups}) or '*' in~ ({ResourceGroups}) or 'value::all' in~ ({ResourceGroups})
| order by name asc
| project value = id, label = tostring(name), group = resourceGroup

content.query:

| extend resourceGroupId = strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup)
| where resourceGroupId in~ ({ResourceGroups}) or 'value::all' in~ ({ResourceGroups}) or '*' in~ ({ResourceGroups})
| where id in~ ({Resources}) or 'value::all' in~ ({Resources}) or '*' in~ ({Resources})
| project ['Logic App'] = name, ['Resource group'] = resourceGroup, Subscription = subscriptionId, Location = location, ['Resource ID'] = id
| order by ['Logic App'] asc
